answers.core:
Automatic instancing was implemented in the Forward+ renderer directly, so it makes sense to do the same for the mobile renderer too.

A more technical reason would be: It's impossible to modify the list of draw commands that the mobile renderer computes from the scene render list via GDScript or GDExtension.
answers.workaround:
Well... You could write your own mesh batcher with a MultiMesh, but you'd also have to deal with culling yourself. This would end up being a fairly complex system, with noticeable GDScript overhead due to having to reimplement culling for each instance.

And of course, such a mesh batcher would not be editable directly in the editor without an accompanying tool script. Really, all the reasons that apply to why Forward+ got automatic instancing should apply here, perhaps even more so as the target platform (mobile devices) is weaker.

title: Implement automatic instancing for the mobile renderer
